judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble is oddly structured: the agreement is said to be made 'by and between' EGL and the Borrower yet 'in favor of' the Facility Agent, and the parenthetical '("EGL" or the "Guarantor" as the case may be)' leaves the two labels imprecisely allocated. Whether the Borrower is a full party with enforceable rights, or merely a signatory acknowledging Article II mechanics, is genuinely arguable on this wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matters directly against Section 4.15, which denies rights to any Person 'other than the Lenders' not a party, and against Section 2.01(a)(ii), which promises Deficiency funds to the Borrower — so whether the Borrower can enforce turns on this recital of parties. That is a live whole-instrument tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain recital that the Lenders agreed to make severally extensions of credit under the Credit Agreement; no term in it carries two meanings. Nothing to construe on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Section 2.01 and the Borrower Obligations definition, which likewise key off the Credit Agreement. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line factual recital of affiliation; 'affiliated group of companies' is loose but does nothing operative. Very little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports the consideration recital and Section 2.01 but imposes no obligation, so nothing in Articles II–IV can contradict it. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Substantial direct and indirect benefit' is a conclusory, vague phrase, though it is standard consideration boilerplate for an upstream guarantee. Some scope for argument about what benefit was in fact derived.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This recital points toward value received while Article III(e) (solvency) and Section 2.01(b)(ii)'s fraudulent-conveyance cap deal with the same subject operatively — a recital-versus-operative-text angle in an insolvency setting. Moderate but not specific.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States a condition precedent to the Lenders' obligation to lend; the words are definite and the 'ratable benefit of the Lenders' formula is conventional. Little room for two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Ratable benefit of the Lenders' sits against Section 2.01(a)(ii)'s promise of funds to the Borrower and Section 4.15's beneficiary limit, but the recital itself does not operate. Mild tension only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration and inducement language with no ambiguous term to name. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the recitals and with Article III's inducement preamble; no operative provision contradicts it. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional incorporation of Credit Agreement definitions qualified by 'unless the context requires otherwise', a phrase that is vague but universally used. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because many operative terms (Commercial Operations Date, Project, Required Lenders, Facility, Parent, Unrestricted Account) are never defined here, this clause carries the whole instrument's meaning off-document, and Section 1.03's priority rule may cut the other way. Some real interaction risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A self-referential definition of 'Agreement' with the usual amendment tail; nothing ambiguous. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.08/4.14 and with all internal 'herein' references under Section 1.02(d). Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is a sprawling catch-all ('all other obligations and liabilities ... whether direct or indirect ... or otherwise') and defines Borrower Obligations by reference to 'the Obligations (as defined in the Credit Agreement)', which makes its outer boundary depend on another document. Breadth plus the enumerated-then-general structure gives some 1.3 exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with the 'Obligations' definition (c014), which loops back to Borrower Obligations, and with the $250,000,000 cap in Section 2.01(a)(iii); the circularity is a genuine, if repairable, internal wrinkle. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (ii) does not parse with the lead-in ('shortfall ... required: ... (ii) any increase in the cost of the Project'), and 'as determined by the Borrower or the Required Lenders', 'any actual shortfall, howsoever caused' and the US$1,097,000,000 threshold each admit of competing readings about when and in what amount a Deficiency exists. This is the sort of short, load-bearing, garbled definition courts are asked to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives Section 2.01(a)(ii) (EGL must fund 'the full and complete amount of any Deficiency') and Section 2.02's notice machinery, and whether the Borrower's own determination binds EGL cannot be reconciled cleanly with Section 2.02(a)'s requirement of an Engineering Consultant certification for lender-issued notices. A specific incoherence exists.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One enormous sentence in which the subject ('an offtake agreement or agreements') is separated from the verb 'becomes effective' by six clauses, and it turns on 'reasonably acceptable', 'arms' length actual purchase' and a good-faith negotiation proviso. The release trigger for the whole guarantee is therefore textually contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the first limb of the termination test in Section 2.01(d) and bounds clause (iii) of Section 2.01(a); a guarantee that can be released by the Borrower procuring an affiliate offtake sits awkwardly with the absolute-and-unconditional language of Section 2.05. Real, nameable tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference definition; nothing in it is ambiguous on its own. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its content depends entirely on Section 2.01(a), which bundles three differently-scoped obligations (including one owed to the Borrower) under one label; that bundling is where any trouble lies. Some derivative exposure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Material adverse effect on ... the business, financial condition, operations or performance or properties of the Guarantor since the date of this Agreement' is both vague and awkwardly time-qualified — the 'since' clause is hard to apply to a representation made on the signing date. The term is classically litigated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds Article III(a), (c), (d) and the notice covenant in (m)(2), and the 'since the date of this Agreement' tail fits poorly with a representation given 'on the date hereof' under the Article III preamble. Modest but identifiable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is circular in effect: 'Obligations' means Borrower Obligations, which are defined as 'the Obligations (as defined in the Credit Agreement)'. Short definitions with that loop invite argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears directly on Section 4.02(c)'s survival of 'the Obligations' and on Section 2.03's payment-in-full condition, and the same defined word carries a different meaning in the Credit Agreement, which Section 1.03 says this Agreement overrides. A specific circularity exists.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sub-clause (e) expressly abolishes ejusdem generis ('a general statement ... shall not be limited to matters similar to the matters specifically mentioned'), which is precisely the general-versus-specific battleground, and it does so with an 'unless otherwise expressly indicated' escape. The rule itself is the thing parties fight about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs how every list in the document (e.g. the Borrower Obligations catch-all and the Deficiency clauses) is read, but no other provision contradicts it. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'For the purposes of and to the extent of the matters covered by this Agreement' is a self-limiting qualifier whose reach is uncertain — almost every matter here is also covered by the Credit Agreement. The scope words are namable and slippery.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely engages Section 2.01(b)'s 'Anything herein or in any other Loan Document to the contrary notwithstanding' and Section 1.01's wholesale importation of Credit Agreement definitions, so which document governs a term like 'Obligations' is genuinely open. Real interaction risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three obligations of different character are crammed into one sentence with a misplaced proviso and a stray comma before '(collectively', leaving it arguable whether the $250,000,000 cap attaches only to clause (iii) or to the aggregate, and clause (ii) runs to the Borrower rather than the Lenders. The period boundaries ('to and until satisfaction of all conditions set forth in Sections 4.01 through 4.02') also overlap with clause (ii)'s period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot be read comfortably with Section 2.07 (payments 'will be paid to the Lenders'), Section 4.15 (no rights to non-Lenders) or Section 2.01(c) (obligations may exceed the Guarantor's liability), and the cap sits against Section 2.01(b)'s 'notwithstanding' language. This is the core operative clause and a likely construction battleground.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (i) is grammatically broken — 'the obligations of the Guarantor hereunder are primary and notwithstanding the obligations of any other Person' has no predicate for 'notwithstanding', so its meaning must be reconstructed. That is a mechanical error affecting sense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its opening 'Anything herein or in any other Loan Document to the contrary notwithstanding' collides with the express $250,000,000 cap in Section 2.01(a)(iii) and with Section 1.03's priority rule, since (ii) sets a different maximum liability measure. A nameable conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, conventional statement that the Borrower Obligations may exceed the guaranteed amount; the wording is clear. Little to construe alone.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes a capped guarantee and so must be harmonised with the $250,000,000 limit in Section 2.01(a)(iii) and the fraudulent-conveyance ceiling in 2.01(b)(ii); harmonisation is straightforward. Modest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Until the earlier of' is precise, but the second limb piles three cumulative conditions into one 'date', and the closing 'notwithstanding that ... the Borrower may be free from any Borrower Obligations' is awkward. Some, not much, textual exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Termination on the EGL Guarantee Release Date must be squared with Section 2.03 (subrogation barred until all Guarantor Obligations paid), Section 2.06 (reinstatement) and Section 2.01(a)(ii)'s pre-Commercial Operations Deficiency duty, which the Release Date definition does not obviously reach. Genuine harmonisation questions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence is ungrammatical ('shall notify the Guarantor ... to the extent a Deficiency at any time exists and that the Guarantor provides to the Borrower the amount'), and it is unclear whether the Engineering Consultant certification attaches only to a Facility Agent notice or to any Deficiency notice. Both are namable defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.01(a)(ii) conditions EGL's funding duty on receiving notice 'as set forth in Section 2.02(a)', while Section 2.02(b) says the Agent and Lenders have no obligation to give notice — so the trigger can fail entirely if the Borrower stays silent. That is a specific internal incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The disclaimer is clear on its own terms, though 'shall not be liable to any party' is broadly drafted in the Agent's favour. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Section 2.02(a)'s mandatory 'The Borrower shall notify' and Section 2.01(a)(ii)'s notice-conditioned duty; read together, the funding covenant can be rendered unenforceable, which is the Lovejoy-style nullification problem. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The subsection is lettered (d) with no (c) in the document, and it speaks of increasing the 'charter capital' of a Minnesota limited liability company, a category mismatch. It also leaves unclear who chooses between equity and an Unsecured Subordinated Promoter Loan.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The missing (c) and (e) leave Article II visibly incomplete, and the election language ('If the Guarantor decides') is hard to reconcile with Section 2.01(a)(ii)'s unconditional duty to provide 'the full and complete amount of any Deficiency'. A real fit problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To pay the cost or cost that has created the Deficiency' is a repeated typographical error whose intended words ('cost or costs') must be supplied, and the subsection is lettered (f) with no (e). Minor but visible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats the elective structure of 2.02(d) and again presupposes a Guarantor choice, which fits uneasily with the mandatory funding limb of Section 2.01(a)(ii). Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but conventional subrogation-waiver language; 'any other Guarantor' is undefined here but its sense is plain enough. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The final carve-out cross-refers to Section 6.07 of the Credit Agreement, an external provision, and the payment-in-full condition tracks Section 2.01(d)(ii); nothing contradicts it. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single very long sentence, but of a standard waiver type whose operation is well understood; no term stands out as bearing two meanings. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces Sections 2.05 and 2.01 rather than cutting against them; no conflicting provision found. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It uses 'a Guaranteed Obligation', a term never defined in Article I, and carves out 'a defense of payment or performance' from an otherwise absolute waiver — the interaction of that carve-out with clause (iii)'s 'any other circumstance whatsoever' is contestable. Namable defects exist.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An unconditional guarantee of payment is hard to square with Section 2.01(d)'s release on the EGL Guarantee Release Date and with the $250,000,000 cap, though those can be read as express exceptions. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is clear in structure but reinstates on the insolvency 'of the Guarantor' only, where reinstatement provisions ordinarily turn on the Borrower's insolvency; the closing 'or otherwise' is an open-ended catch-all. Some intrinsic exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That Guarantor-only trigger fits poorly with Section 2.01(d)'s termination mechanics and with the Borrower-centric definition of Borrower Obligations (which expressly contemplates the Borrower's bankruptcy). A nameable mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single short sentence; 'without set-off or counterclaim in Dollars' is definite. Little intrinsic ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says payments 'will be paid to the Lenders', while Section 2.01(a)(ii) requires the Deficiency amount to be provided 'to the Borrower' by capital contribution or subordinated loan under Section 2.02(d) — a direct clash on payee. Also cuts against the Guarantor's set-off authorisation in Section 4.04.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lead-in says only that the Guarantor 'represents and warrants', with no covenant language, and the repetition date formula ('on each other date on which representations and warranties are made or deemed made under the Credit Agreement') imports an external schedule. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article III as headed covers 'Representations, Warranties and Covenants', and subsections (h), (l), (m), (n) and (o) are plainly covenants introduced by a representations-only preamble; Section 4.07 forbids using the heading to cure that. A concrete internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard organisation and good-standing representation; 'duly qualified as a foreign corporation' is odd for a Cayman company but conventional. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses Material Adverse Effect as defined in Section 1.01 and conflicts with nothing else in the instrument. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional power-and-enforceability representation with the usual bankruptcy and equitable-principles qualifications; nothing genuinely two-sided. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'each other Loan Document to which it is a party', consistent with Sections 1.03 and 4.08; no contradiction found. Low.
